tiles.name: Rocky dirt
tiles.explanation:
Rocky dirt is noise: lumps of light and dark scattered so the eye reads a texture, not shapes. The lumps here are clusters of a few pixels in the lighter browns on a dark ground. They do not run off one edge without carrying on from the opposite edge, so copies join without a seam.

![Rocky dirt, repeated](examples/fill-repeated.png)

Repeated 9 times, though, the same lumps line up in rows and columns, and the eye finds the grid. The next two tiles fix that.

tiles.name: Sparse dirt
tiles.explanation: A variant tile uses the same colors with fewer lumps. Mixed in among the first tile, it breaks up the grid: the eye stops finding the same shape every 16 pixels.

tiles.name: Boulder
tiles.explanation:
The third tile has a big boulder in the lightest browns. Use a tile like this rarely: one landmark among plain tiles makes the ground look natural, but used everywhere it becomes the new repeating pattern.

![The three tiles mixed](examples/mixed.png)
